title: Kernel context fingerprinting and span harmonization for prefill/decode telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a low-overhead, unified mapping from runtime NVTX/kernel markers into trace spans and per-kernel metrics that supports both high-cardinality analysis (heatmaps by kernel variant) and low-cardinality alerting (SLO regressions).

Motivation: current telemetry has scattered NVTX ranges and inconsistent span names across prefill and decode codepaths, making it hard to aggregate per-kernel latency and resource usage. That impedes our ability to detect regressions introduced by kernel selection or attention optimization changes and to answer questions like "which kernel variant causes tail latency spikes during long-context prefill?".

Key proposal:
- Introduce a compact kernel fingerprint tag emitted at kernel-launch time: kernel_family:kernel_variant:opsig. This is a short string (e.g., matmul:f16_shmm:KxNx64) emitted to NVTX and as an attribute on trace spans.
- Harmonize span naming: use outer spans for logical phases (prefill, decode, kv-fetch, attention) and child spans for kernel-level work using the fingerprint as the child span name and as a metric label. Span name pattern: phase.kernel_family.kernel_variant.
- Emit per-kernel metrics as histograms and counters: duration_ms_histogram, tokens_processed, flops_estimate, and launch_count. Tag these metrics with model_id, sequence_length_bucket, device_type, and kernel_fingerprint.
- Sampling & aggregation strategy: full traces are sampled at 1% by default; kernel-level metrics are exported for every invocation but with adaptive aggregation on the agent: cumulative histograms per-second and 1m rollups to avoid high cardinality in Prometheus. Provide an OTLP export pathway for high-fidelity traces during investigations.
- Backfill plan: add migration layer to map old NVTX names to new fingerprints to preserve historical continuity in dashboards and alerts.

Implementation notes:
- Instrument a single kernel-launch wrapper in the serving runtime so NVTX push/pop and span start/stop are colocated. This reduces instrumentation duplication and ensures consistent attributes.
- Avoid heavy per-kernel allocations: reuse a small ring buffer of fingerprint strings and use preallocated histogram buckets. Keep CPU overhead <1% p99 under typical workloads in microbenchmarks.
- Integrations: export to existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Cortex) with a new ingestion transform that collapses sequence_length into buckets and normalizes kernel_fingerprint values to reduce cardinality. Also export traces to our tracing backend (Jaeger/OTLP collector) for sampled traces.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Full-trace capture for every request gives maximum resolution but is too expensive; we compromise with sampled traces + full per-kernel metrics.
- Storing raw kernel signatures in metrics increases cardinality risk; mitigate by fingerprint normalization and bucketing.
- Using NVTX alone is insufficient for aggregation since NVTX labels differ by caller; pairing NVTX with span attributes is necessary.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline emits kernel_fingerprint-tagged histograms and spans for both prefill and decode.
- Dashboards show a new per-kernel latency heatmap and a sequence_length vs kernel_variant pivot in observability console.
- Overhead measured in perf job stays under 1% mean CPU and <2% p99 CPU, and adds <2ms p99 latency to single-request cold-paths in our QA harness.
